title: zanthoxylum budrunga var. rhetsa
intro: Zanthoxylum budrunga var. rhetsa, commonly known as Indian pepper, is a plant species belonging to the Rutaceae family. It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to treat various health conditions, with documented health benefits including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which contribute to its ability to alleviate pain, reduce fever, and protect against infections. The therapeutic actions of Indian pepper include its analgesic, anti-arthritic, and anti-ulcerogenic effects, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as alkaloids, flavonoids, and terpenes. The bioactive constituents of Zanthoxylum budrunga var. rhetsa have been identified as including alkaloids like berberine and palmitic acid, as well as flavonoids like quercetin and kaempferol, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
